editorial:
Imagine being in Los Angeles back in the day when punk rock was just starting to blow up. You get to follow Darby Crash, a guy with a huge ego and a wild vision who forms the band The Germs. Along with his bandmates Lorna Doom, Pat Smear, and Don Bolles, he tries to shake up the entire music scene. The vibe is gritty, loud, and messy, perfectly capturing that feeling of being young and reckless. You will see how Darby pushes everyone around him to the limit just to make his mark on the world, which makes for a really intense ride.

The acting feels real, and you can tell the creators cared about the true story. One big pro is how it handles the music, but the pacing can feel a bit slow in some spots. If you love stories about troubled artists or the early days of rock, you will dig this. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a high-quality digital copy.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a sad note as Darby Crash's life falls apart. After reaching a peak of fame in the underground scene, his drug use and mental struggles take over. He eventually takes his own life, leaving his bandmates and friends behind. It wraps up by showing how he became a legend in the punk world, but only after losing everything he had in real life. It is a heavy finish that shows the cost of his ambition.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music history and true stories about rock stars.
